description: The fabric's own hygiene list, applied to every slice, skill and prompt section in every project, beside the credential and language checks in tools/fabric/layout.py and each project's .agent-fabric/hygiene.json. A person is named by role, never by name — the CEO, the owner, an agent by its login: a distilled slice travels into every project's repository and a name in it is a privacy matter, not a style one (decided 2026-09-16). refer_as says what the corpus says instead. A GitHub owner is named only if it is an organization on the owner list the four GitHub patterns share (a personal handle is a privacy matter like a name); a URL is read on the hosts whose first path segment is the owner (github.com, www., gist., codeload., raw. and gist.githubusercontent.com, and after repos/, users/, sponsors/ or LFS media/), never on GitHub's API root or its other sites; each matches the owner alone, so the drain's <owner> leaves the URL or reference readable. Not read, because a path looks the same: a bare owner/repo in prose or a heading, a repo label, gh's -R, a variable such as REPO=owner/repo, a gh api path after a flag that ends in no API resource the fourth pattern lists; Written by fabric-coordinator.

patterns.label: an account or handle built from a person's name (a GitHub login, a Claude account, a key's variable) -- name it by whose it is
person's name -- refer to the CEO by role
private-network address (10.0.0.0/8) -- say 'a private address' or name the role
private-network address (192.168.0.0/16) -- say 'a private address' or name the role
private-network address (172.16.0.0/12) -- say 'a private address' or name the role
a /home/<login>/ path -- write the path from the repository root or ~/
host scratch path -- name the artifact by commit, sha and how to rebuild it; a path on one host's volatile volume is gone after a wipe and means nothing elsewhere
one account's scratch path -- name the artifact by commit, sha and how to rebuild it
a GitHub URL under an owner that is no listed organization -- a personal handle is a privacy matter, as a name is: write <owner>, or add an organization to the owner list the GitHub patterns share

an <owner>/<repo>#N reference under an owner that is no listed organization -- a personal handle is a privacy matter, as a name is: write <owner>, or add an organization to the owner list the GitHub patterns share

patterns.pattern: (?:(?<=--repo )|(?<=--repo=)|(?<=--repo ")|(?<=--repo=")|(?<=--repo ')|(?<=--repo=')|(?<=gh api repos/)|(?<=gh api /repos/)|(?<=gh repo clone )|(?<=gh repo view )|(?<=gh repo fork )|(?<=uses: ))(?!(?:BlueTeam-OU|gzapi-org|github|actions|docker|apache|alibaba|The-PR-Agent|deepseek-ai|google-research|herdrdev|laude-institute|mozilla-ai|oxc-project|project-minigraf|router-for-me|rtk-ai|shcherbak-ai|tinyhumansai|z-galaxy|owner|o|testorg)(?![\w-]))[A-Za-z0-9][\w-]*(?![\w-])(?=/[A-Za-z0-9])
patterns.label: a --repo, gh repo or uses: argument, or a gh api repos/ path, under an owner that is no listed organization -- a personal handle is a privacy matter, as a name is: write <owner>, or add an organization to the owner list the GitHub patterns share

an API path repos/<owner>/<repo>/<resource> under an owner that is no listed organization -- a personal handle is a privacy matter, as a name is: write <owner>, or add an organization to the owner list the GitHub patterns share
